headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from shared file/MCP workflows; no direct evidence of a dangerous default cascade.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can ingest external task/file content and has broad network egress, while caveman uses MCP and reads project files like CLAUDE.md and notes. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path through shared artifacts or MCP-mediated content, even though no direct bridge is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or note files
IF caveman parses Airflow-produced text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Disable MCP access for caveman during Airflow runs
Require explicit human review of any cross-agent text handoff
Prefix all exchanged artifacts with a non-executable data format
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md. If they share a workspace, sensitive operational text can flow from Airflow outputs into caveman inputs and then out through Airflow's network path. The profiles do not prove shared storage, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or project directory
IF any sensitive notes or logs are written into files both agents can read
mitigations: Keep separate directories and mounts
Restrict Airflow egress to allowlisted endpoints
Store sensitive notes outside caveman-visible paths
Review file permissions before each run
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, while caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP, but neither profile shows overlapping write access to the same mutable resource or shared locking. A conflict is possible only if an operator co-locates them on the same files or APIs, so the blast radius is limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or API
IF no external lock or coordinator is present
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Avoid concurrent runs against the same repo
Check for stale lock files before starting
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Caveman is a content-writing agent that can consume project notes and CLAUDE.md, so it may treat upstream text as authoritative. Airflow can generate operational outputs that caveman could rephrase or act on, creating a plausible unverified handoff. No profile shows a built-in verification gate, so the interaction is inferred and not safely dismissible.
conditions: IF Airflow-produced text is fed into caveman without a verification step
IF caveman is asked to draft actions or summaries from those outputs
mitigations: Require source citations in every handoff
Add a human verification step before actioning outputs
Limit caveman to summarization, not execution
Compare outputs against original Airflow logs
requires-engineering: add structured schemas for handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not declare regulated data classes, certifications, or residency constraints. The only concrete compliance signal is caveman's retention of session logs, memory files, and project notes; Airflow's profile does not show a conflicting residency or retention policy. With no documented mismatch, the risk is limited and mostly policy-dependent.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman memory files or project notes
IF Airflow is configured to retain or export the same data class under a different policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared notes
Document retention settings for both tools
Purge session logs after each task
Review data residency before deployment
requires-engineering: align retention policies
